players.product: Quantinuum quantum computing customer and innovation partner in pharmaceuticals

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Robert Bradway: Q2 2026 total revenues exceeded $10 billion, a 10% year-over-year increase; 22 products delivered double-digit sales growth and 17 products annualized at more than $1 billion based on Q2 sales.
quarterly_data.figure: total revenues exceeded $10 billion, a 10% year-over-year increase

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Amgen's 6 key growth drivers grew at an aggregate rate of 26% year-over-year and represented nearly 70% of Q2 product sales (EVP Worldwide Commercial Murdo Gordon: Repatha +37%, EVENITY +38%, TEZSPIRE +42%, Rare Disease +21%, Innovative Oncology +18%, Biosimilars +29%).
quarterly_data.figure: 6 key growth drivers +26% YoY, nearly 70% of Q2 product sales

quarterly_data.signal: Repatha (EVP Murdo Gordon): Q2 sales $953 million, growing 37% year-over-year; U.S. new-to-brand prescriptions growing more than 50% year-over-year; more than 1 million people in the U.S. are on Repatha (CEO). Murdo Gordon: roughly half of the growth comes from cardiologists broadening use and the other half from primary care physicians treating high-risk primary prevention patients, notably patients with diabetes.

Repatha (R&D President Jay Bradner): from VESALIUS-CV, for patients with high-risk diabetes with and without atherosclerosis Repatha reduced 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events by 29% and produced a nominal 21% reduction in the risk of all-cause death; based on VESALIUS-CV Amgen recently received a positive CHMP opinion supporting a broader label for Repatha in the EU.
quarterly_data.figure: 3-point MACE reduced by 29%; nominal 21% reduction in all-cause death

quarterly_data.signal: Repatha vs the newly approved oral PCSK9 (EVP Murdo Gordon): the two labels 'really just don't compare'; additional therapies are 'not necessarily competing for share with Repatha', and the oral label carries food restrictions in the first 30 minutes after dosing.

EVENITY (EVP Murdo Gordon): Q2 sales increased 38% to $714 million, after 27% growth in the previous quarter; in the U.S. about 2 million women are at very high risk of a fracture with EVENITY at only mid-single-digit penetration; in Japan EVENITY holds more than 55% volume share and 1 million patients have been treated.

TEZSPIRE (EVP Murdo Gordon): Q2 sales grew 42% year-over-year to $486 million, driven by severe uncontrolled asthma, where it was the market leader in new-to-brand prescription share among allergists; uptake in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps is encouraging. R&D President: the Phase III study in eosinophilic esophagitis is expected to complete in the second half of the year.
Prolia and XGEVA (EVP Murdo Gordon): combined Q2 sales of $1.1 billion, a decrease of 33% year-over-year, in line with expectations given several biosimilar competitors have launched.

Rare Disease (EVP Murdo Gordon): portfolio grew 21% year-over-year to $1.6 billion; UPLIZNA sales increased 90% to $335 million across all 3 approved indications, with a doubling of U.S. gMG prescribers since the previous quarter.

TEPEZZA (EVP Murdo Gordon): Q2 sales grew 14% to $576 million; launched in 13 countries with an additional 6 planned in the coming months; more than 25,000 U.S. patients treated since approval; Phase III data for the subcutaneous on-body injector showed efficacy comparable to IV TEPEZZA.

Innovative Oncology (EVP Murdo Gordon): portfolio grew 18% to approximately $2 billion in Q2; IMDELLTRA sales increased 115% to $288 million with over 2,000 U.S. accounts using it; BLINCYTO sales increased 23% to $472 million with 64% growth outside the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: Innovative Oncology approximately $2 billion, +18%; IMDELLTRA $288 million, +115%; BLINCYTO $472 million, +23%

quarterly_data.signal: Biosimilars (EVP Murdo Gordon): portfolio grew 29% to $855 million in Q2; PAVBLU (EYLEA biosimilar) sales increased 121% to $287 million; the portfolio has generated more than $15 billion in sales since the first approvals in 2018; next-wave candidates for EYLEA HD, OPDIVO, KEYTRUDA and OCREVUS are in late-stage clinical development.

MariTide (R&D President Jay Bradner): 9 ongoing and 3 additional planned Phase III studies across obesity and related chronic diseases; Phase III uses a 3-step dose escalation reaching target dose in 2 months, then monthly dosing, with maintenance studies testing as few as 4 or 6 doses per year and a dedicated Phase III switch study from weekly GLP-1 therapies; the intact molecule's half-life is approximately 21 days. Amgen stopped development of AMG 513, a Phase I obesity asset.
quarterly_data.figure: 9 ongoing and 3 planned Phase III studies

quarterly_data.signal: Olpasiran (R&D President Jay Bradner): greater than 95% Lp(a) reduction in Phase II; 2 ongoing Phase III outcome studies (primary and secondary prevention); OCEAN(a) enrolled 7,297 patients requiring Lp(a) above 200 nmol/L, with every-12-week dosing and a 3-point MACE primary endpoint. On competitor pelacarsen data, Bradner expects 'perhaps some directional insight, but not decisional perspective', citing 95% Lp(a) reduction compared to, say, 70% for that molecule.

UPLIZNA pipeline (R&D President Jay Bradner): in the 1-year open-label extension of the Phase III MITIGATE study in IgG4-related disease, after an 87% reduction in flare risk versus placebo in year 1, 100% of patients who continued treatment remained flare-free at year 2 and 71.4% achieved complete remission without glucocorticoids; Amgen initiated the registrational MERCURY study in autoimmune hepatitis (up to 150,000 U.S. patients) and plans a Phase III study in CIDP (about 35,000 U.S. patients).

Dazodalibep (Sjogren's disease): two dedicated Phase III studies (symptomatic and systemic disease) with results expected later this year (R&D President Jay Bradner: 'we'll learn more about dazodalibep in H2 of this year'); management said the Phase III studies have 621 patients in the systemic study and 434 in the symptomatic study.
quarterly_data.figure: 621 systemic and 434 symptomatic Phase III patients

quarterly_data.signal: Sunakiment (formerly AMG 104, inhaled anti-TSLP Fab; R&D President Jay Bradner): in the Phase II LEVANTE dose-ranging study the primary endpoint (CompEx at 12 weeks) was not statistically significant, though numerical reductions were observed; Amgen is planning a Phase III program with AstraZeneca.

IMDELLTRA and BiTE pipeline (R&D President Jay Bradner): 3 Phase III studies in earlier treatment lines are underway, which could allow IMDELLTRA to reach as many as 28,000 addressable U.S. patients; new Phase III DeLLphi-315 evaluates subcutaneous tarlatamab; monitoring has come down from 16 hours in the second-line Phase III to 1 to 2 hours in some current experience; Xaluritamig is in two Phase III studies in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
quarterly_data.figure: as many as 28,000 addressable U.S. patients

quarterly_data.signal: R&D President Jay Bradner on AI: Amgen recently established a frontier AI laboratory in Amgen research combining advanced models with proprietary data, bringing agentic workflows to discovery research; AI is applied across discovery, development, manufacturing and access.

CFO Peter Griffith: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin 48%; non-GAAP R&D spending up 10% year-over-year; non-GAAP cost of sales 19.6% of product sales (higher profit sharing, royalties and mix); free cash flow $3.5 billion in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: non-GAAP operating margin 48%; free cash flow $3.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 capital expenditures of $500 million, driven by U.S. manufacturing sites including North Carolina, Ohio and Puerto Rico; Amgen continues to expect capital expenditures of approximately $2.6 billion in 2026 to scale manufacturing capacity for volume growth, including for MariTide's launch.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 capex $500 million; 2026 capex approximately $2.6 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Amgen raised its 2026 guidance - total revenues now $38.2 billion to $39.4 billion and non-GAAP EPS $22.30 to $23.50; non-GAAP operating margin still roughly 45% to 46% of product sales.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenues $38.2 billion to $39.4 billion; non-GAAP EPS $22.30 to $23.50

quarterly_data.signal: CFO 2026 outlook details: other revenue approximately $1.9 billion; non-GAAP R&D expense to grow high single digits (including 9 ongoing global Phase III MariTide trials and a business development transaction that will increase non-GAAP R&D expense in Q3); non-GAAP other income and expense $2.1 billion to $2.2 billion of expense; non-GAAP tax rate 15.0% to 16.5%; a meaningful sequential increase in operating expenses expected in Q3.

Otezla (EVP Murdo Gordon): used as a first-stop systemic agent; new entrants are competing with each other after Otezla rather than directly with it; 'some pressure on price' from 340B exposure, but volume 'is actually holding up quite good'.

CEO on business development: Amgen is looking at external opportunities 'primarily in smaller earlier-stage assets' in its 4 therapeutic areas; the strategy is not directly linked to the late Phase III readouts.
